newsitem.title: USA: Drugs slow perishable shipments through Miami.
newsitem.headline: Drugs slow perishable shipments through Miami.

text.p: Illegal drugs coming into Miami International Airport are a big obstacle to getting delicate perishable goods though the airport quickly, several speakers told a conference here this week.
"Drugs are a big cause for added delays at Miami International Airport," Bill Spohrer, president of Challenge Air Cargo said.
Speakers described how every box of flowers coming through the airport must be X-rayed, which slows down getting the fragile blooms to market in Europe and the United States.
"The airlines are working hard to combat" the drugs, Spohrer said.

Challenge not only has the X-ray equipment, but also employs drug-sniffing dogs, video equipment and other methods to check for illegal drugs, he told those gathered at a perishables logistics conference sponsored jointly by Miami International Airport and the Frankfurt Airport.

Despite the industry's anti-drug efforts, U.S. Customs seized 1,774 pounds of illegal drugs in boxes of flowers at the Miami airport last year, Mary Martins, Miami-based chief of the U.S. Customs Service Anti-Smuggling unit said. One-third of the amount was found by the air carriers' own efforts, she added.
Martins said the carriers pushed the Customs service to the next level by urging them to look into the various suppliers and contractors such as caterers.
Martins also announced a new anti-drug initiative called the Business Anti-Smuggling Coaltion, which she described as a public-private sector partnership.

The new coalition is being tried out in Laredo, Texas and San Diego, California as well as Miami. It targets the manufacturers and shippers of goods. "We are trying to keep the dope out of the importers products," Martins said.
The airlines are charged a $1,000 per ounce fine for cocaine or other drugs found in shipments handled by the airlines, Spohrer said.
"There is so much money in drugs, it corrupts everything it touches," Spohrer said, commenting on how difficult it is to keep drugs out of the flower shipments, a favored vehicle for drug smugglers.
The fines and extra security measures are "passed along to everyone down the chain to the final consumer," he said.
The conference is the first cooperative marketing effort by the two airports. Both airports are huge perishable shipping points.
